newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Krupp warns against softening EMU criteria.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Krupp warns against softening EMU criteria.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp on Monday warned the entry criteria for Europe's planned currency union (EMU) may not be watered down as this would make it more difficult to create stability.

"If the criteria were watered down, then currency stability could be reached only with great problems," Krupp, also president of the state central bank in Hamburg, Schleswig-Holstein und Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, said.
Krupp also said it would make little sense to allow nations to join the union, set to begin on January 1, 1999, who have not met the entry criteria.

To join the union, nations must meet several criteria, showing that the budget deficit does not exceed three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) and that government debt does not exceed 60 percent of GDP.
For Germany it is particularly important that the currency union will be able to prevent another strengthening of the mark and stop the loss of jobs, Krupp said.
The mark's recent strength was made partly responsible for German firms' struggle to export goods which became suddently more expensive, Krupp added.
"Consequently Germany needs parameters for the currency union which cannot be changed," Krupp said.
